name: cloudflare-pages-migration
what_it_does: Walks through moving a website from its current host onto Cloudflare Pages, keeping the old host live until the new one is proven, and changing one DNS record rather than the whole domain.
what_you_say: move this site to Cloudflare Pages
what_you_get: The migration carried out step by step, with the commands and their real output shown, including a comparison of the old and new site.
on_your_computer: Runs Cloudflare's `wrangler` tool and the AWS command-line tool on your computer under sign-ins you already have, changes one DNS record in your domain's settings, and fetches both the old and new site to compare them.

name: deploy-verify-fix
what_it_does: Runs your project's own deploy, checks the result at the address a visitor would use, works out what went wrong from the real output, and redeploys, round after round.
what_you_say: deploy this and keep going until it actually works
what_you_get: A working deploy, or a diagnosis and a recommendation if it does not converge, plus a one-line record of each round.
on_your_computer: Runs the deploy, verification and rollback commands your project has already defined, edits your project files to fix what it finds, and reaches the address it is verifying over the internet.

name: deploy-loop-owner
what_it_does: Takes over a whole deploy job and keeps going on its own, so you are not carrying files back and forth between the work and the place it has to run.
what_you_say: take this to staging and don't come back until it's verified
what_you_get: A verified deploy, or the diagnosis and a recommendation, never a file handed back for you to try.
on_your_computer: Nothing restricts which tools it uses, so it can run commands, change your project files and use the network by itself until it succeeds or hits one of the two stop points in its instructions.
